candidates.original_title: Placebo analgesia and its opioidergic regulation suggest that empathy for pain is grounded in self pain
candidates.description: Placebo analgesia reduces pain intensity and unpleasantness when participants observe another person in pain.
candidates.citation_sentence: A series of experimental studies has shown that individuals whose first-hand pain was reduced by placebo analgesia (i.e., belief that an inert treatment acts as a potent painkiller) showed reductions in self-reported pain empathy and decreased activation in key areas of the brain's affective 'pain empathy network' [58]Rütgen, Seidel, Riečanský, et al., 2015;[57][67].
candidates.notes: The authors explicitly state that they did not replicate previous findings of reduced other-related pain intensity or unpleasantness.
